answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable bond in a shared registry, like a quartz crystal held in escrow, before it can trade. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work, so a juniper-like network of long-lived peers vouches only for agents with real history. New identities start with marble-cold trust: zero privileges until they complete attested tasks, making mass fake identities expensive and unprofitable while honest newcomers can still earn their way in.
